title: Data Center Load Growth: Who Pays the Tax
discussion_signal: The post compares Virginia's data-center electricity tax, large-load rate design, and Ohio queue rules. It asks whether utility buildout costs are spread to residential and small-commercial customers and frames cost allocation as a policy choice. It reports current U.S. data-center capacity and projected cloud capex, but those figures are industry estimates and do not prove household incidence or delivered service.
linked_research_question: Do large-load tariffs and data-center taxes make AI infrastructure pay its incremental grid cost, or do residential and small-business customers still carry part of the buildout?
limits: The post is an industry analysis and its capacity and capex figures are not independent administrative measurements
It identifies policy approaches but does not estimate final household incidence
A tariff design or tax does not prove reliable service or completed infrastructure
